narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: Tells the story and introduces each speech.

eliu.name: Eliu
eliu.note: Son of Barachel the Buzite; the angry young bystander who speaks after the three friends fall silent.

2.t: Doth thy thought seem right to thee, that thou shouldst say: I am more just than God?

3.t: For thou saidst: That which is right doth not please thee: or what will it profit thee if I sin?

4.t: Therefore I will answer thy words, and thy friends with thee.

5.t: Look up to heaven and see, and behold the sky, that it is higher than thee.

6.t: If thou sin, what shalt thou hurt him? and if thy iniquities be multiplied, what shalt thou do against him?

7.t: And if thou do justly, what shalt thou give him, or what shall he receive of thy hand?

8.t: Thy wickedness may hurt a man that is like thee: and thy justice may help the son of man.

9.t: By reason of the multitude of oppressors they shall cry out: and shall wail for the violence of the arm of tyrants.

10.t: And he hath not said: Where is God, who made me, who hath given songs in the night?

11.t: Who teacheth us more than the beasts of the earth, and instructeth us more than the fowls of the air.

12.t: There shall they cry, and he will not hear, because of the pride of evil men.

13.t: God therefore will not hear in vain, and the Almighty will look into the causes of every one.

14.t: Yea, when thou shalt say: He considereth not: be judged before him, and expect him.

15.t: For he doth not now bring on his fury, neither doth he revenge wickedness exceedingly.

16.t: Therefore Job openeth his mouth in vain, and multiplieth words without knowledge.
